title: Increment/decrement operators, and side effects
recap: Prefix increment changes its operand and yields the changed value. Postfix increment also changes its operand but yields the value from before that change; decrement has the same prefix and postfix distinction.
Increment and decrement have side effects. Prefer one mutation per statement and avoid expressions that modify and read the same object in ways whose sequencing is unclear or undefined.
objectives: Observe the value produced by postfix increment.
Observe the value produced by prefix increment.
Apply prefix decrement as a separate statement.
Keep each side effect simple and sequenced.
warnings: Do not assume prefix and postfix forms produce the same expression value.
Do not increment the same variable multiple times in one expression.
Use ordinary assignment when no increment/decrement behavior is being practiced.
challenge: Start a ticket counter at 5. Capture its old value with postfix increment, then capture its new value with prefix increment, and finally decrement the counter once in a separate statement. Report both captured values and the final counter.
hints: Initialize postfixValue with counter++; counter changes to 6 after yielding 5.
Initialize prefixValue with ++counter; counter changes to 7 before yielding 7.
Put --counter; on its own statement before printing the final value.
